transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-11-19
Start: 09:20 PST
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Liu (Redwood CSM), Samantha Reed (Itera Head of Data), Jordan Kim (Itera SRE), Carlos Vega (Itera CTO)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in to review onboarding progress, confirm access (S3/IAM, kms), discuss KMS/encryption, and schedule a performance run on Dedicated capacity. Agreed action items and target dates.

00:00 - Alex Moreno: "hey everyone, thanks for joining, it's alex here from Redwood, we've got priya on the se side and mark joining for cs. how's everyone doing this morning?"
00:07 - Samantha Reed: "good morning, thanks alex, doing well, busy week but ready to go."
00:12 - Carlos Vega: "morning — quick heads up, i might need to jump at 10:00 for another call but i'll stick around for the main items."
00:18 - Priya Shah: "great, agenda for today: quick onboarding checklist sync, access status (s3/iam, kms), vpc peering progress, and then schedule the perf run plus any outstanding security questions."
00:30 - Jordan Kim: "yep that's right — we focused last week on getting the s3 bucket right and making sure iam roles are scoped. i've got a couple of questions about the role permissions for the redwood agent."
00:40 - Alex Moreno: "cool, priya do you want to cover the current access matrix?"
00:45 - Priya Shah: "sure. status: redwood service account created (redwood-poc@iteraha-prod), we need the customer to attach the RW S3 policy we sent. also we need the assume-role trust policy to allow our inference nodes in the dedicated pool to read the KV cache and models from the bucket. i've pasted a terraform snippet in the doc, but i can also send a stripped down example."
01:02 - Samantha Reed: "i saw the snippet, quick q: is cross-account role required if we use a peered vpc? i thought peering might handle it."
01:10 - Priya Shah: "peering helps for network traffic but the S3 access is still IAM-based; cross-account role with proper trust is the cleanest, otherwise you'd need to open the bucket which we advise against."
01:22 - Jordan Kim: "ok we'll do the assume-role approach. i'll run that with our infra team. i need the exact ARN though and the minimal policy. priya can you send the minimal policy?"
01:30 - Priya Shah: "yes, will send — action for me. note: there's a small typo in the doc where 'kv-cache' appears as 'kvcache' — sorry earlier transcription got weird, but policy examples are correct in the repo."
01:44 - Alex Moreno: "also on KMS, we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, you'll want to create a key and grant decrypt/encrypt to the role. mark, can you add the KMS note?"
01:55 - Mark Liu: "yeah, quick note: we recommend CMK with key policy that allows Redwood's service principal or the role you created. if you need HSM-level, let us know and we can route to our enterprise team."
02:08 - Carlos Vega: "is that compatible with our on-prem HSM? we have some regs that push for HSM-backed keys for certain PHI datasets."
02:16 - Priya Shah: "we support KMS and we have integrations for external key management in Private deployments — there are a few more steps but it's supported. we'll include the architecture doc in the security packet."
02:30 - Alex Moreno: "okay network/VPC — where are we with peering? jordan?"
02:35 - Jordan Kim: "we started the peering request, network team has a couple questions: 1) CIDR overlap check (no overlap), 2) route tables updated, 3) is there a preference for site-to-site or transit gateway? we were thinking TGW is cleaner long-term."
02:48 - Priya Shah: "for most customers we recommend TGW for scale, but peering works for POC. if you expect multi-region or many VPCs, TGW is better. for the perf run TGW isn't required strictly."
03:01 - Samantha Reed: "we'll do peering for now to keep it simple — easier to approve. jordan will coordinate the route table changes. also, what about egress for model downloads?"
03:12 - Priya Shah: "model artifacts will be pulled from S3. if peering is in place and IAM is set, the nodes will pull over the private link. otherwise models can be cached on the node image in advance."
03:22 - Alex Moreno: "perf run — we proposed a dedicated pool run with 50 concurrent inference sessions to match your expected load. priya, what's the rough ETA for us to run that once access is granted?"
03:33 - Priya Shah: "we can run it within 48 hours of access + sample data availability. we'd prefer a small representative dataset ~10k records. we need the sample data and the S3 read role to run realistic KV cache warmups and batching patterns."
03:50 - Jordan Kim: "timeline sounds fine. i'll aim to provide the S3 path and role by monday (2025-11-24)."
04:00 - Samantha Reed: "i can get the sample records ready, question on redaction — do you need PHI? we'll send synthetic or de-identified data."
04:10 - Priya Shah: "synthetic is perfect for perf. for quality checks we might want de-id examples but not raw PHI in the POC environment unless the Private deployment and contractual DPA are in place."
04:25 - Alex Moreno: "security docs — we will send SOC2, encryption details, and our incident response summary. mark will attach the SLA PDF. expect a doc drop by friday (2025-11-21)."
04:36 - Mark Liu: "i'll share the link in the repo after the call. also there's an audit log sample if you want to see the event format for requests and token usage."
04:48 - Carlos Vega: "pricing — sam asked me to be sure we understand commit options for Dedicated. alex can you outline quick?"
04:55 - Alex Moreno: "short: we have pay-as-you-go in hosted, and reserved monthly/annual for Dedicated with discounted unit costs. i'll send the pricing sheet and a couple commit tiers that match your expected qps. sending by 2025-11-22 as an action."
05:10 - Jordan Kim: "another technical: what about KV cache priming? if we have a cold start will latency spike a lot?"
05:16 - Priya Shah: "there's a warmup strategy — we prime the KV based on request prefixes and you can also prepopulate with the sample dataset. for Dedicated we can keep KV in memory across sessions to keep tail latency low."
05:30 - Alex Moreno: "any blockers from your side that would prevent the perf run?"
05:34 - Samantha Reed: "main blockers: IAM role not yet attached, S3 path to sample data, and final peering confirmation. nothing blocking us contractually at this stage."
05:44 - Carlos Vega: "we also want to confirm data residency — our corp policy asks that logs stay in us-east-1. can you guarantee region placement for the Dedicated nodes?"
05:55 - Priya Shah: "yes we can pin the Dedicated pool to a region, we'll note us-east-1 in the perf cluster request. our private deployment options also allow stricter residency if needed."
06:08 - Alex Moreno: "recap and next steps: Priya to send minimal IAM policy and terraform snippet by Friday; Alex/Mark to share SOC2, KMS doc, SLA PDF by Friday; Jordan to grant role and share S3 ARN by Monday (24th); Samantha to upload sample dataset by Monday; schedule perf run for 26th. agree?"
06:30 - Samantha Reed: "agree."
06:34 - Jordan Kim: "agree, i'll flag questions in the ticket."
06:38 - Carlos Vega: "sounds good, thanks everyone."
06:42 - Alex Moreno: "thanks all, we'll follow up in email and repo. mark will post the security pack link."
06:50 - Priya Shah: "one tiny note — we noticed some names of the redwood products in the doc getting auto-corrected, e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' turned into 'Red wood' in one doc, ignore that, correct copy will be in the repo."
06:58 - Mark Liu: "posting links now in the meeting chat: security_whitepaper.pdf, soc2_summary.pdf, sla_dedicated.pdf (links in repo)."
07:10 - Alex Moreno: "okay we'll wrap — next sync same time next week unless you want mid-week for the perf results."
07:18 - Samantha Reed: "let's do a quick follow-up after perf run, a separate 30-min slot works."
07:24 - Alex Moreno: "perfect. thanks everyone, talk soon."
07:28 - (call ends)
